sa-mus-musculus.title: Fancy Mouse
sa-mus-musculus.summary: Small, busy and social, pet mice live in complex groups and should be kept with familiar companions of the same sex. They're more for watching than cuddling.
rows: About 2–3 in (5–8 cm) body length for pet mice; show mice are larger

A roomy, escape-proof cage (mice squeeze through tiny gaps) away from direct sun, heat and noise. At least 2 cm of bedding (cellulose or non-aspen wood chips; no fine sawdust), nest material, ropes, tubes and a solid wheel
Mouse nuggets as a complete diet, with small amounts of fruit and vegetables within the daily ration; scatter some to encourage foraging
Keep in stable same-sex groups of familiar mice (ideally siblings); don't add or remove members. Males can be aggressive to unfamiliar males
A prey species; get them used to you gently before handling
Most active at night and around dawn and dusk
warn: Mice are very sensitive to heat; keep the cage out of direct sun.
